title: Nonvanishing of a pulled-back invertible section
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], $N$ an invertible module on $Y$ [def-sc-invertible-module], $t$ a global section of $N$, and $x\in X$. Restrict $t$ with the unit of the canonical tensor-pullback adjunction [def-pc-module-pullback] [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction]. Then $x$ belongs to the nonvanishing locus of that pulled-back section if and only if $f(x)$ belongs to the nonvanishing locus of $t$ [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module].

source.place: Sheaves Tag 0098, Properties Section 01PR, residue-value criterion

proof.text: The quotient-tensor isomorphism identifies one tensor a germ in the residue-field fibre with its class modulo the maximal ideal times the whole stalk module. Thus residue value zero is equivalent to membership in that submodule; this is the complement of the definition of nonvanishing.

Apply the fibre comparison clause of [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor]. It carries the residue value of the pulled-back section to one tensor the original residue value. Extension of scalars between fields is faithfully flat, so one tensor a vector is zero exactly when the vector is zero. Transport this equality through the fibre isomorphism and negate the zero-value equivalence.

lean.statement: theorem nonvanishing_tensorPullback {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (N : Y.Modules) [N.IsInvertible] (t : Γ(N, ⊤)) (x : X) : let adj := Classical.choose (exists_tensorPullbackAdjunction f) let res : Γ((tensorPullback f).obj N, ⊤) := (adj.unit.app N).val.app (op ⊤) t x ∈ nonvanishingLocus ((tensorPullback f).obj N) res ↔ f x ∈ nonvanishingLocus N t
